cohort: The study included pregnant women at the extremes of reproductive age (adolescents aged <=19 years and women older than 35 years) and their newborns from the Brazilian public health network.
finding: Pregnant women of advanced age presented a higher frequency of cesarean deliveries compared to adolescent women.
mod_finding: Pregnant women of advanced age had a higher frequency of cesarean deliveries (54.6%) compared to adolescent women (38.7%).
cross-section timing: Data was collected on pregnant women and their newborns, implying observations around the time of birth.
birth_weight: Low birth weight infants were an outcome, and birth weight was collected as perinatal data.
gest_age: Preterm births, small for gestational age (SGA), and large for gestational age (LGA) were outcomes, and gestational age was collected as perinatal data.
